newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - Apr29.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - Apr29.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Coca-Cola is testing a poster advertising campaign in Hungary that will supplement the brand's traditional red colour with brown and green. If the strategy works in Hungary it may be introduced all over the world. (Vilaggazdasag, April 24, 1997)
-- McCann-Erickson is running a massive TV and print advertising campaign in the Czech Republic for Haslerky cough drops with liquid filling. (Strategie, April 1997)

-- The Hungarian parliament is debating a bill to regulate tobacco advertising, but a recent survey suggests that restrictions on tobacco advertising could cut state revenues by 4.2 billion forints ($23.2 million), while press advertising income could drop by 2.5 billion forints within three years. (Vilaggazdasag, April 24, 1997)

-- Czech mobile phone operator EuroTel spent more than 100 million crowns ($3.3 million) on advertising last year, while rival RadioMobil spent about half that amount. The advertising battle between the two is expected to hot up in the autumn, when RadioMobil's coverage will equal EuroTel's. (Strategie News, April 16-23, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- The Czech parliamentary commission for media is against the possible takeover of Prima Television by Nova Television, which would mean the end of competition in Czech broadcasting. However, the commission has no power to stop it. (Lidove Noviny, April 22, 1997)

-- The Hungarian telecommunications company Matav Rt will launch commercial Internet services on May 5. The number of individual Internet subscribers in Hungary amounts to 10,000, but Matav hopes the figure will grow to 50,000 by the end of the year. (Napi Gazdasag, April 23, 1997)

-- Czech doctors will have free access to the Internet through the medical information system MediClub. They will be able to read medical literature in the World Wide Web's virtual library, receive information about pharmaceutical companies and products, and will have access to world medical databases. (Lidove Noviny, April 22, 1997)
-- A new homes and interiors magazine called Moderni Byt and published by Renata Film 1 will hit Czech news stands at the end of April. (Strategie News, April 16-23, 1997)

-- The live broadcast of news conferences and political comment on the night of the Bulgarian general election would not have been possible without the sponsorship of major advertisers, National Television said. (24 Chasa, April 24, 1997)
-- The Polish Nowe Zycie Gospodarcze economic weekly is planning a share listing on the Warsaw bourse by the end of 1998. (Parkiet, 22 April, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Czech brewer Plzensky Prazdroj is planning an extensive media campaign to support its Gambrinus and Pilsner Urquell brands and plans to invest between 50 and 60 million crowns in marketing. (Pravo, April 21, 1997)
-- Ford introduced the Ka -- its latest small car -- in the Czech Republic this month, backed by an extensive ad campaign on TV and in magazines. (Strategie News, April 16-23, 1997)
-- Hungarian retailers are selling dairy products past their "sell by dates" or without adequate cold storage facilities, a survey by consumer watchdog FVF has found. (Vilaggazdasag, April 23, 1997)

-- Cosmetics company Avon Products Inc has built a $5 million distribution centre in Hungary. Avon's sales in Hungary have soared by 70 percent in the last three years. (Vilaggazdasag, April 23, 1997)
-- Around 75 percent of adult Poles buy beer, and lager sales are growing at the fastest rate, a survey by the Indicator market research agency said. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, April 21, 1997)
